title: Only 8% Pass This Paramedic Entrance Exam
summary: Scene safety, vital signs, emergency maths and rapid-response judgement get harder across 10 stages.

landing.intro: From scene hazards and vital signs to emergency maths and calm communication, prove you can think clearly when every clue matters.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.explanation: The heart contracts to move blood through the circulation.

questions.question: Which observation changed while the others stayed the same?

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse unchanged, breathing increased, alertness unchanged, skin warmth unchanged

questions.explanation: Breathing changed from 16 to 24 while every other recorded observation stayed the same.

questions.question: Four sealed packs hold five dressings each. How many dressings are there?
questions.explanation: Four groups of five contain 20 items in total.

questions.question: A live electrical cable lies across the only doorway. What comes first?
answers: Move it with a dry object
Ask a bystander to watch it
Keep everyone clear and get qualified help to make it safe
questions.explanation: A live cable creates an immediate scene hazard; nobody should approach or handle it until qualified help makes the area safe.

questions.question: Which opening makes the clearest handover?
answers: At 14:20, breathing became faster and alertness decreased
Here are all the minor details in random order
I already know exactly what caused it
questions.explanation: A time plus two clearly observed changes gives the next person concise, useful information without making unsupported assumptions.

questions.question: Which takes priority?
questions.context: A routine equipment checklist is due soon. At the same time, a person who was comfortable becomes pale, dizzy and less responsive.
answers: Complete the routine checklist before responding
Prioritise the person’s sudden deterioration and seek qualified help
Wait until the checklist deadline has passed
Choose whichever task is physically nearest
questions.explanation: A sudden change in colour, dizziness and responsiveness takes priority over routine administrative work.

questions.question: Which route correctly follows oxygen into the circulation?
questions.explanation: Air travels through the airway to the lungs, where oxygen crosses into the blood.

questions.question: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart into the circulation.

questions.question: Which body system carries signals between the brain and the rest of the body?
questions.explanation: The brain, spinal cord and nerves form the communication network of the nervous system.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the kidneys?
answers: They exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide
They remove wastes from blood and help regulate water balance
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter the blood, remove wastes and help regulate the body's water and electrolyte balance.

questions.question: Which body-function detail changed?
questions.context: Earlier, both hand grips were equal. Now the right grip is unchanged, but the left grip is weaker than before.
questions.explanation: The visible comparison shows a new reduction in left-hand grip strength.

questions.question: Which concern has the highest priority?
questions.context: The person's chest is moving, but very little air movement can be detected and they cannot speak normally.
answers: A possible airway or breathing problem needing immediate qualified assessment
questions.explanation: Minimal air movement plus difficulty speaking points to an immediate airway or breathing concern.

questions.question: How many millilitres are in 1.25 litres?
questions.explanation: Multiplying 1.25 by 1,000 gives 1,250 mL.

questions.question: How much time passes from 14:35 to 15:20?
questions.explanation: There are 25 minutes to 15:00 and another 20 minutes to 15:20, making 45 minutes.

questions.question: What is the combined recorded volume?
What is 30% of 200?
questions.explanation: Thirty per cent of 200 is 0.30 × 200, which equals 60.

questions.question: You count 8 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the rate per minute?
questions.explanation: Thirty seconds is half a minute, so doubling 8 gives 16 breaths per minute.

questions.question: Which message should be communicated first?
questions.context: One message confirms a routine arrival time. A second reports new heavy bleeding and that the person is becoming faint.
answers: The routine arrival time, because it came first
The new bleeding concern, because it may signal urgent deterioration
Neither message until every detail is available
questions.explanation: New heavy bleeding plus faintness is more urgent than a routine timing update.

questions.question: A person is beside moving traffic with no protected working area. What is safest?
answers: Walk into traffic and wave vehicles around
Ask the person to cross the road immediately
Keep clear, identify the danger and seek appropriate scene support
Place equipment in the road to slow vehicles
questions.explanation: Moving traffic is an immediate environmental hazard; the area must be made safe before anyone enters it.

questions.question: A cable is sparking beside a metal fence. What should you do?
answers: Pull the cable away by its covering
Touch the fence briefly to test it
Pour water over the sparking point
Keep everyone clear and get qualified emergency help
questions.explanation: Sparking electricity near metal may energise the surrounding area; nobody should touch or approach it.

questions.question: Broken glass and a used sharp object are on the floor. What is the safest response?
answers: Keep people away and arrange safe handling through the proper trained process
Pick everything up with bare hands
Kick the items under nearby furniture
Leave the sharp unmarked for someone else
questions.explanation: Sharps should not be handled casually; isolate the hazard and use an appropriately trained safe-disposal process.

questions.question: A task may expose the face and hands to splashing body fluid. What guides PPE choice?
answers: The colour of the equipment bag
The assessed exposure risk, including hand and eye or face protection
questions.explanation: Standard Precautions select PPE according to the anticipated exposure to blood or body fluids.

questions.question: A bystander starts discussing a person's private details where others can hear. What is best?
answers: Repeat the details so everyone understands
Move the conversation to a private setting and share only necessary information
Post the information on a public notice
questions.explanation: Privacy and dignity require sensitive information to be discussed discreetly and only when necessary.

questions.question: Smoke is coming from a building and someone inside can be heard coughing. What comes first?
answers: Open every door without checking conditions
Ask an untrained bystander to go inside
Stay clear of the unsafe building and alert appropriate emergency help
questions.explanation: Smoke makes the scene unsafe; entering could create additional casualties, so specialist emergency help is required.

questions.question: Which observation was recorded as 76?
questions.explanation: The observation card recorded the pulse as 76.

questions.question: Which measurement changed while the others stayed the same?

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse unchanged, breathing increased, alertness unchanged, skin warmth unchanged

questions.explanation: Breathing increased from 16 to 25 while the remaining observations stayed unchanged.

questions.question: Which newly recorded change matters most?
questions.context: Earlier the person was alert and answered promptly. Now they are drowsy and respond much more slowly.
answers: The time written on the card
questions.explanation: A new reduction in responsiveness is a significant change from the person's earlier condition.

questions.question: What is the best interpretation of this pattern?
questions.context: Across three checks the pulse rises from 80 to 92 to 108. The person also becomes pale and dizzy.

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse 80 then 92 then 108, with pallor and dizziness

answers: The symptoms can be ignored because no diagnosis is shown
The combined trend suggests deterioration needing prompt qualified assessment
questions.explanation: A rising pulse together with new pallor and dizziness is a combined pattern of deterioration.

questions.question: Why can reduced breathing affect working tissues?
answers: Less oxygen can enter the blood and reach the tissues
The kidneys stop receiving nerve signals
questions.explanation: Breathing supplies oxygen to the lungs; reduced gas exchange can reduce oxygen delivery through the blood.

questions.question: Who needs attention first?
questions.context: Person A feels well and their observations remain steady. Person B is newly clammy and dizzy, and their pulse has risen across three checks.
answers: Person A, because their observations were recorded first
Person B, because several changes point to deterioration
Both can wait because neither has a named diagnosis
The person with the shorter name
questions.explanation: Person B has multiple new changes and a worsening trend, making them the priority.

questions.question: A person says, “I'm terrified.” Which response is best?
answers: There is nothing to be scared about
Try not to think about it
I can see this is frightening. Tell me what worries you most
I guarantee everything will be fine
questions.explanation: The response acknowledges the emotion and invites the person to explain their concern.

questions.question: A person nods but appears not to understand your explanation. What should happen next?
answers: Repeat the same technical words more quickly
Assume a nod always means understanding
Use plain language, suitable communication support and check understanding
questions.explanation: Clear language, appropriate communication support and a check-back confirm whether the message was understood.

questions.question: Someone needs to discuss a sensitive health concern. What protects dignity?
answers: Find a private setting and listen without making assumptions
Ask them to explain in front of everyone
Tell nearby people the concern first
questions.explanation: A private setting and non-judgemental listening protect confidentiality and dignity.

questions.question: A person asks, “Am I definitely going to be okay?” What is the best response?
answers: Avoid unsupported promises, listen and explain what can be said clearly
Give a diagnosis without enough information
questions.explanation: Honest, compassionate communication avoids false reassurance while keeping the person informed.

questions.question: A coughing person is sharing a small waiting area. Which general safety action fits the visible risk?
answers: Turn off all ventilation without assessment
Encourage respiratory and hand hygiene and follow risk-based precautions
questions.explanation: Respiratory hygiene, hand hygiene and risk-based precautions are core infection-prevention measures.

questions.question: Which detail belongs first in a concise handover?
questions.context: Earlier the person was alert. At 16:20 they became newly confused and their breathing became faster.
answers: An unrelated event from last week
Every normal detail before mentioning the change
The new confusion, faster breathing and the time the change occurred
questions.explanation: A concise handover leads with the important new change and when it occurred.

questions.question: Who needs attention first?
questions.context: Person A has ankle pain, is comfortable and speaks normally. Person B is suddenly confused, breathing rapidly and looks pale.
answers: Person B, because several new signs suggest sudden deterioration
Person A, because pain always comes first
Both can wait until every form is completed
questions.explanation: Person B has combined breathing, circulation and mental-status changes that require immediate attention.

questions.question: Which situation takes priority?
questions.context: Person A requests a blanket and is speaking comfortably. Person B has new breathing difficulty and cannot finish a sentence.
answers: Whichever request was made more loudly
questions.explanation: New breathing difficulty severe enough to limit speech is the immediate priority.

questions.question: Who needs attention first?
questions.context: Person A has a mild headache that is unchanged. Person B briefly collapsed and is now clammy, dizzy and unusually weak.
answers: Person A, because headaches are always urgent
Neither person, because both are awake
Person B, because collapse plus new circulation-related signs suggests deterioration
The person who can answer most questions
questions.explanation: A recent collapse combined with clamminess, dizziness and weakness makes Person B the priority.

questions.question: Which body-system concern needs immediate qualified assessment?
questions.context: Person A has temporary tingling after resting on one elbow and moves normally. Person B develops sudden one-sided weakness and a new speech change.
answers: A routine digestive concern in Person A
A minor skin concern in Person B
A bone-growth concern in Person A
A possible brain or nervous-system problem in Person B
questions.explanation: Sudden one-sided weakness and a speech change together indicate an urgent nervous-system concern.

questions.question: Which observation pattern needs attention first?
questions.context: Person A's pulse rises after stairs, then returns towards their earlier level. Person B's breathing becomes faster across three checks and they become drowsy.
answers: Person B's worsening breathing trend with reduced responsiveness
Neither pattern matters because only trends are shown
questions.explanation: Person B shows both a worsening breathing trend and a decline in responsiveness.

questions.question: Which communication need comes first?
questions.context: Person A asks repeated questions because the area is noisy and relaxes when things are explained. Person B says a violent person is nearby and they do not feel safe.
answers: Continue the conversation where everyone can hear
Move towards safety and communicate the immediate safety concern
Tell Person B to ignore the concern
Discuss Person A's questions before addressing danger
questions.explanation: An immediate safety concern must be communicated and addressed before routine explanation continues.

questions.question: Which organ coordinates the nervous system?
questions.explanation: The brain processes information and coordinates activity through the nervous system.

questions.question: What is 25% of 80?
questions.explanation: Twenty-five per cent is one quarter, and one quarter of 80 is 20.

questions.question: 08:40 to 09:05?
questions.explanation: There are 20 minutes to 09:00 and five more to 09:05.

questions.question: Which record shows a rising trend?
questions.explanation: The values 16, 20 and 24 rise at each successive check.

questions.question: Heavy shelf tilting overhead?
questions.explanation: A falling-object risk makes the immediate area unsafe; move clear and prevent others from entering it.

questions.question: They look confused after your explanation.
questions.explanation: Rephrasing in plain language and checking understanding responds directly to visible confusion.

questions.question: Which body-function detail changed?
questions.context: HANDOVER NOTE — Earlier: both arms raised equally. Now: the right arm stays raised, but the left arm drifts down. Both legs still move equally.
questions.explanation: The new left-arm drift is the only changed movement described in the handover.

questions.question: How much time passed before arrival?
questions.context: INCIDENT TIMELINE — Dispatch recorded: 14:10. Arrival recorded: 14:28.
questions.explanation: From 14:10 to 14:28 is 18 minutes.

questions.question: What total distance belongs in the record?
questions.context: INCIDENT RECORD — One access route measures 0.4 km. A second section measures 250 m. Write the combined distance in metres.
questions.explanation: 0.4 km is 400 m; adding 250 m gives a combined distance of 650 m.

questions.question: Which missing detail matters most for scene safety?
questions.context: SCENE HANDOVER — A vehicle is stationary. Two people are nearby. A strong fuel smell was noticed but not included in the spoken handover.
answers: The fuel smell and possible ignition hazard
questions.explanation: A strong fuel smell may indicate an immediate scene hazard and must be communicated clearly.

questions.question: Which safety step was missed?
questions.context: INFECTION NOTE — Gloves were removed after contact with body fluid. A shared radio was then handled before hand hygiene was performed.
answers: Perform hand hygiene before touching shared equipment
Keep the same gloves on for every task
Place the radio on the floor
Skip hand hygiene because gloves were worn
questions.explanation: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene, which should occur before clean shared equipment is handled.

questions.question: Which sentence is the clearest concise handover?
questions.context: HANDOVER DETAIL — At 10:20, breathing became faster and the person became newly confused. Both changes are new.
answers: Things changed at some point and there were several details
At 10:20, breathing became faster and the person became newly confused
The room was quiet before something happened
There are many normal details to discuss before the new changes
questions.explanation: The correct sentence states both important changes and the time they occurred without distraction.

questions.question: If shallow breathing reduces gas exchange, what downstream effect follows most directly?
questions.context: Use the process: air reaches lungs → oxygen enters blood → blood supplies working tissues.

visual.ariaLabel: Shallow breathing, less gas exchange, unknown, less oxygen to tissues

questions.explanation: Reduced gas exchange means less oxygen enters the blood, so less can reach working tissues.

questions.question: What is the best interpretation of the complete trend?
questions.context: Check 1: breathing 16 and alert. Check 2: breathing 22 and anxious. Check 3: breathing 28 and drowsy.

visual.ariaLabel: Breathing 16 alert, then 22 anxious, then 28 drowsy

answers: The values can be ignored because no diagnosis is named
Breathing is worsening while responsiveness is declining
questions.explanation: The breathing rate rises across checks while alertness falls, producing a clear worsening pattern.

questions.question: What combined volume should be written in millilitres?
questions.context: The record contains 0.65 L and 350 mL. Convert the units, then calculate the total.

questions.question: What is the safest response to the combined hazards?
questions.context: INCIDENT RECORD — An aggressive person is throwing objects near the entrance. Equipment partly blocks the nearest exit route.
answers: Approach and argue until the person stops
Keep clear, move others towards a safer route and alert appropriate help
Retrieve the equipment beside the person before leaving
Ask an untrained bystander to block the thrown objects
questions.explanation: Thrown objects and a blocked exit create immediate danger; increase distance, use a safer route and communicate the hazard.

questions.question: Which response protects privacy and checks understanding?
questions.context: The person says, “I do not want this discussed where others can hear, and I still do not understand why you are asking.”
answers: Continue the discussion where everyone can hear
Avoid explaining and ask the same questions again
Move to an appropriate private setting, explain plainly and check understanding
Ask a bystander to explain on your behalf
questions.explanation: A private setting protects dignity, while plain language and a check-back address the person’s lack of understanding.

questions.question: Who needs attention first, and why?
questions.context: Person A has a sore wrist, normal speech and steady observations. Person B briefly collapsed and is now pale, breathing rapidly and newly confused.
answers: Person A, because wrist pain is easier to see
Neither person until a diagnosis is available
Person B, because collapse plus breathing, circulation and mental-status changes suggest deterioration
questions.explanation: Person B has multiple time-sensitive signs across several systems, making them the clear priority.

profiles.title: The Emergency Standout
profiles.copy: You combined excellent foundational knowledge with calm, evidence-led judgement across the entire response assessment. Scene hazards, changing observations and communication details stayed clear even when the final cases became demanding.

profiles.title: The Rapid-Response Natural
profiles.copy: You showed a strong feel for the knowledge and judgement behind safe emergency response. Most of the assessment's trend, numeracy, safety and handover traps did not pull you off course.

profiles.title: The Calm Scene Solver
profiles.copy: You handled a broad mix of body knowledge, scene decisions and multi-clue cases with steady reasoning. A few finer handover and observation details kept the entrance challenge interesting.

profiles.title: The Steady Responder
profiles.copy: You built a solid result by following visible evidence and treating safety seriously. Your strongest stage shows where your emergency-learning instincts are already taking shape.

profiles.title: The Promising Candidate

about.body:
This Rapid Response Assessment turns entrance-level paramedic knowledge into ten increasingly demanding stages. The questions cover anatomy and physiology, emergency numeracy, observation trends, scene safety, infection prevention, calm communication, handover and multi-clue prioritisation.

The challenge is designed for curious adults, prospective paramedic students and emergency-care learners around the world. It uses universal principles such as recognising immediate hazards, noticing deterioration, protecting dignity, communicating clearly and seeking appropriately qualified help—never country-specific protocols or specialist treatment decisions.

Your final percentage reflects only the answers given in this entertainment quiz. It is a playful snapshot of the entrance areas that felt strongest and the topics that proved more challenging, not a judgement of clinical competence or suitability for paramedic practice.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer six questions in each stage and choose the single response best supported by the visible information.
Correct answers stay hidden while you play, so inspect every scene clue, timeline, trend and handover carefully.
Complete all ten stages to reveal your Paramedic Score, strongest entrance area and full answer review.
